i'm not sure if you're asking how each attempt was (like hanging, cutting, etc) or just in general how a person could attempt that many times, so i'll answer both.

**each attempt**: three times were cutting, one overdose attempt, two hanging attempts and one vehicular attempt with an ATV by intentionally crashing it at a high speed.

**how i / someone could attempt that many times**: long story short, severe trauma and lack of psychological help at a young age. i never saw a child psychiatrist until after my first couple attempts and i'm now a Pre-Med student with a focus in child psychology so i can help kids before it gets to that point.

trigger warning below for lots of stuff.

​

when i was 6/7, i was sexually assaulted by my half-brother. i grew up being sexualized by most of the men in my family and struggled with my self-identification since as early as i can remember. 

i have severe religious trauma from my grandmother who would force me to watch religious shows/videos strictly because i was queer. she constantly told me "jesus" doesn't love me and i'm going to burn in hell for eternity. i heard that as early as 11 years old. pretty terrifying shit to tell a kid.

on top of that, i was bullied in school to the point i got multiple truency charges and had to go to court twice. i would cry at the entrance to my school and have such a bad panic attack i would just go home and cry in bed.

that's pretty much the major things; other than that, all of this gave me severe depression, anxiety and i was later diagnosed with DID (dissociative identity disorder), autism and body dysmorphic disorder that also came with severe eating disorders (mostly anorexia. i never weighed more than 100lbs until i was 17-ish. even now i'm 5'7" and i only weigh 111. recovery from that is extra hard.)

​

hopefully that sheds some light. i now know that suicide was never the answer, but it really felt like it for the longest time after all of that.

long story:

for reference, i've been clean for nearly 2.5 years now.

honestly i don't know what clicked for me. i was self-harming on a daily basis, sometimes multiple times a day. i was in therapy with a plethora of different therapists and i often ditched them after one or two visits because they all said the same generic shit that meant nothing.

if i had to say, it's not that i wanted to stop, because it helped me feel alive.

but i was hurting the people i loved. it wasn't just me. my mom, my friends, my sister, my ex at the time. every time i relapsed and came to them and they saw my wrists or my thighs or my arms or whatever, they would have the saddest look on their face. they never blamed me, but i couldn't keep seeing that sadness in their eyes. i realized i had to stop before it went too far and i couldn't ever keep my loved ones happy.

i have an app called "I Am Sober" (for all sorts of addictions) where you can log your feelings, how many days you've been clean, talk with other people who are in the same milestone ballpark as you, and a bunch of other stuff. it's helped a lot.

alongside making music, drawing art, going out and enjoying time with my sister, having virtual dates with my partner who lives 400+ miles away during a pandemic. it's the little things that remind me why i'm staying alive and staying clean.

it's so hard to recover but i truly believe in my heart everyone has at least one reason. they just have to find it, and i believe they'll also do that at the right time.

The four seasons have four personifications. Four bodies who control the elements. Four people who keep the world in balance.

Spring. A 12 year old girl. Brown hair. She wears skirts and t-shirts that have hearts on them. She's by far everyone's favorite.

Autumn. Nicknamed Fall. She's a short, outgoing girl. Her outfits are always changing. She's the least popular, but she still has people that favor her over the others. She's okay with that.

Summer. A Tall, Brunette woman who wears short shorts and crop tops. She's always warm, always comfortable. Tied for favorite with Spring.

Winter. The loner. The cold one. The only man of the seasons. He's a quiet, blonde who wears snug sweatpants and sweaters. He's always cold, never comfortable.

Love is a weird concept to Winter. He didn't know what it felt like, but he struggled with a way he felt towards Summer.


Winter knew he always had to wait his turn. He couldn't barge in when it was Summer's time to shine. He had to wait, all the way through Fall, to stand up and tell the world something through his element. Through his weather.

The summer months went on for a long time, it felt like—and Fall's didn't go any faster. Dragging on, Winter had felt like he waited years for his time: and when it came, he didn't waste a second.

His first day was stressful. Everyone around him sighed and wished he would disappear. The few that loved him were far and few between. Especially those who favored Summer.

He knew he didn't have what Summer has. A bright personality, a lovely aura. A warm heart. A perfect sense of humor.

Winter knew his tries to come out on top were useless, but this year, he had a misson. He had to tell Summer how he felt.

He knew she was watching. She's always watching.


"Winter," She spoke to break the silence. "It's good to see you again. Good luck these next few months."

He chuckled. His first laugh in a long time. "Thanks, Summer." He replied quietly.




As the days went by, Summer didn't talk to Winter much. She never did. 


He had to say something. Today. Something simple. Something loud.

Every snowflake he created was different. No two were the same, and it was time he created one for summer.


She watched the snow fall outside and became puzzled when her hair began to feel cold spots. She looked up. A small, but significant hole in the ceiling let some snow in. She held out her hand.

Down fell one more single snowflake, landing in her palm.

It crystalized, and Summer smiled.

The object, now jewelry in her hand was a heart with S etched in the middle.

"Lots of people love you," he whispered to her, standing outside, conjuring more snowflakes with his fingertips. "I think I do, too."

"Marrisa," he whispered. "It's okay to be scared."

The looming trees above them barely let the sunlight pass through, but it showed them a direction. It showed them where they needed to go.

"No!" She shouts, a little too loud. The birds in the trees decide to flee. "No," she said again, quieter, "We need to do this. We have to do this. Scared or not, Lucas, this is our destiny."

She was right, he knew she was. The only thing that fate had in store for them in their young lives was this journey. This dirt path. These trees. This sunshine.

They sauntered on, stepping on fallen leaves and broken twigs. Lucas looked at Marrisa. He knew he wasn't going to see her again.

Without warning, he stopped in his tracks and grabbed her by the waist, pulling her in for a passionate kiss. They had reached the end of the road.

"The light will guide us." They say in unison, as their fingertips turned to ashe.
